objectives: Explain the purpose and scope of MCP and the integration problem it standardizes between AI applications and external systems
Describe the core MCP concepts of hosts, clients, servers, primitives, and the stateless JSON-RPC request model
Reason about interoperability, protocol versioning, and the value of one open protocol over per-system custom integrations
Read the MCP specification, its revision history, and its feature lifecycle to tell current, deprecated, and removed behavior apart
Read the schemas and structured data that define MCP messages, tool definitions, capabilities, and server manifests
Distinguish the responsibilities of MCP hosts, clients, and servers and how discovery and capability negotiation connect them
Trace the model interaction flow from a user request through the host, model, client, and server and back into model context
Apply the request, notification, subscription, and multi round-trip interaction patterns and handle each result type
Handle protocol errors and tool execution errors, including version, capability, header, and validation failures
Walk the tool invocation lifecycle from discovery and selection through call, user input, progress, cancellation, and result
Identify the protocol primitives and utilities, including tools, resources, prompts, completion, caching, pagination, transports, and deprecated client features
Locate the trust boundaries between host, client, server, model, and the tools and content a server exposes
Apply OAuth-based authorization, client registration, scopes, and user consent so a user approves what a server may see and do
Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
Design auditability and observability so protocol activity can be traced, attributed, and reviewed
Map the roles, responsibilities, governance, and adoption patterns of teams building and deploying MCP
Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
Reason about ecosystem portability across clients, servers, SDKs, extensions, gateways, and registries
